Berezivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Berezivka, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably founded in the late 19th or early 20th century, this cemetery preserves tombstones from 1915-1918, including one marking a man 'killed by anarchists in 1918'; it appears on a 1927 Russian map using 1910s data and was ruined during WWII, though some prewar tombstones survive, and it remained in use until the 1990s. Berezivka's Jewish community is first mentioned in the first half of the 19th century; an April 26-27, 1881 pogrom damaged 161 Jewish-owned buildings, sparing only the synagogue and pharmacy. Population reached 3,458 (56%) by 1887. A Soviet-era Yiddish elementary and evening school, club, and library operated alongside artisan cooperatives and Jewish kolkhozes; population fell to 3,223 (43%) by 1926 and 1,424 by 1939. Wehrmacht occupation from August 10, 1941 saw 211 Jews murdered by September; after the town's inclusion into Romanian Transnistria, thousands of Bessarabian and Odesa Jews were also deported to the Berezivka area, with nearly 7,000 killed in total. Epigraphic evidence confirms a Jewish population persisted in Berezivka until 1989.
